1952, August 20
The following is a faithful transcription of the typed original by the Servant of God, Father Solanus Casey, O. F. M. Cap.
Pax Et Bonum St. Felix Friary Huntington, Indiana
1952, August, 20 th
Feast of Saint Bernard. Blessed be God in all His designs. Mr. Philip R. O'Brien
Bailey's Harbor, Wisconsin
God Bless you Mr. Philip R. O'Brien:
God bless you and yours these days of grace. For days of grace are these our days and days of God's great mercy to all men of good will, notwithstanding our lamentable want of appreciation and of gratitude for His inestimable graces and His uncountable favors. Days of grace too, notwithstanding the threatening avalanche of international red-atheism even now be- deviling millions of humanity more and more brazenly and presump- tuously aspiring on earliest opportunity, "to-take-over" for rel- igion. Nay - in places behind the "Iron Curtain", actually taking over and, instead of keeping highest promises, is doublly grind- ing its dupesinto abject slavery of body and soul: while at the same time it is going to the limit of its power in trying to play Hell with every decent subject who dare profess other than what tends to kill true religion and belief in the Supernatural.
Atheism! God help us! "The social octupus-cancer of mind and spirit"! Atheism? The no-God-monster proposition, when philosophy and commonsense as well (as) revelation and faith in the Eternal -all- proclaim, "appreciation and grati- tude for favors received, the very first and surest indication of intelligence."? Atheism; the stifler of every phase of science that down the ages has fostered gratitude to parents and bene- factors as to God's representatives and that, instead of, "Hope, the very soul of happiness in this world", would inject the poi- sonous nightmare of eternal despair? Aye! Aye! God help us these days of God's grace and mercy, against the atheism of Anti- christ: -- atheism the unqualified climax atonce, of intellectual insanity, of moral degeneracy, of diabolical blasphemy and of et- ernal despair. God help us!
Pardon me Dear Mr. O'Brien I hope this is not boring you, but it seems to me that, when we behold the general outlook in the material and materialistic world today and the inordinate tendency of thot-less humanity to worship this passing existence as though it were our final destiny and the only life worth striving for (unfinished draft.)
